$comment: What every binding (the Node.js addon and the web module) must expose. Checked by `mise run surface`, which `mise run test` runs: each public function of include/tinyactors/*.h is "bind" (it survives linking every binding with dead-code elimination from its entry points), bound for some bindings with a reason for the others, or skipped with a reason; each typings file declares every runtime export and public class member of the module it describes. A new TA_API function fails the check until it is classified here.

ta_trace_context_child.skip: a C host's helper for the traceparent of a step's children; the JS bindings get it formatted on peer effects (traceparent) and build one with formatTraceparent

ta_trace_body_size.skip: for C hosts that copy records; the bindings hand records to the OTLP encoder (ta_otlp_read), which reads bodies itself

ta_core_deliver.skip: kernel-only embedding (bring your own scheduler); the bindings embed ta_system

ta_core_instance_size.skip: kernel-only embedding; the bindings embed ta_system

ta_core_step.skip: kernel-only embedding; the bindings embed ta_system

ta_core_workspace_size.skip: kernel-only embedding; the bindings embed ta_system

ta_datamodel_environment_charge.skip: the native datamodel's JavaScript is not metered: the core charges each datamodel call a fixed fuel cost, and the run loop bounds a call by its rounds (RUN_ROUNDS x RUN_BUDGET in bindings/node/src/system.c and bindings/web/native.mjs)

ta_datamodel_environment_chart.skip: the bindings' datamodels keep the chart of each instance themselves

ta_datamodel_environment_image.skip: the bindings' datamodels keep the image of each instance themselves

ta_datamodel_null.skip: bound implicitly: ta_system_init adds the null datamodel when the host does not

ta_datamodel_ecmascript_binding.skip: the bindings wrap the C datamodel's vtable (ta_datamodel_ecmascript_vtable) to note which sessions took events and to keep their last variables, so they build their own binding

ta_datamodel_ecmascript_js_runtime.skip: for C embedders adding their own globals; the JS bindings expose the core, and add nothing to the engine

ta_datamodel_ecmascript_payload_from_jso.skip: payloads cross between JavaScript and the C datamodel as neutral values, through its vtable's from_wire

ta_datamodel_ecmascript_payload_to_json.skip: payloads cross between the C datamodel and JavaScript as neutral values, through its vtable's to_wire

ta_datamodel_ecmascript_payload_eval.skip: payloads come from JavaScript values (neutral values through from_wire), not from expressions outside a session

ta_datamodel_ecmascript_set_memory_limit.skip: the bindings set the engine's limit once, at createSystem({ memoryLimit }) (ta_datamodel_ecmascript_config.memory_limit)

ta_datamodel_ecmascript_wasm_set_time.skip: the clock of the C ECMAScript datamodel in wasm (browser_wasm.c), which has no clock of its own; the Node.js addon's engine reads the operating system's

ta_host_route_reason.skip: the reason's text for C transports; the JS transports name reasons on the wire themselves (err frames)

ta_host_state_value.skip: the web binding's JavaScript computes state values until it becomes the wasm twin of the addon (docs/adr/0008-bindings-only-do-io.md)

ta_image_event_name.skip: event names reach the bindings as strings (events, effects, _event); the interned name table serves C datamodels and tools

ta_image_ahead_of_time_section.skip: ahead-of-time sections are read by C datamodels; JS datamodels resolve expressions from their source text

ta_http_encode_post.skip: BasicHTTP codec for C hosts without an HTTP stack; JS hosts have fetch/http

ta_http_parse_request.skip: BasicHTTP codec for C hosts without an HTTP stack; JS hosts have fetch/http

ta_runtime_compile_file.skip: OS convenience for C hosts (files); JS hosts read files with their platform

ta_runtime_now_ns.skip: OS convenience for C hosts (clock); JS hosts supply their platform's clock

ta_runtime_resolve.skip: OS convenience for C hosts (file resolver)

ta_runtime_run.skip: OS convenience for C hosts (run with automatic growth); the bindings grow on TA_RUN_EXHAUSTED themselves

ta_runtime_system_free.skip: OS convenience for C hosts (malloc'd systems)

ta_runtime_system_grow.skip: OS convenience for C hosts; the bindings relocate with ta_system_relocate

ta_runtime_system_new.skip: OS convenience for C hosts (malloc'd systems)

ta_system_next_deadline.skip: the next deadline comes with every ta_system_run result (ta_run.next_deadline), which is when the bindings schedule

ta_system_chart_stats_get.skip: the bindings run a ta_host and read per-chart counts host-wide (ta_host_chart_stats), which sums every segment's with this function

ta_system_set_next_serial.skip: for hosts that allocate session ids outside the system (the PostgreSQL binding); ta_host partitions ids per segment itself (and keeps them past the ids of sessions it adopted)

ta_wasm_alloc.skip: a wasm module's own allocator: the web binding places what it hands the libraries with it; the Node.js addon is native code and has no wasm memory

ta_wasm_free.skip: see ta_wasm_alloc: the web binding gives its blocks back with it; the Node.js addon has no wasm memory
